messages:
tara: @olivia FYI — ACME reported 429s exactly at their monthly window boundary. They say credits went to 0 then immediate 429 for ongoing requests. customer_org: acme-inc, host tz: America/Los_Angeles :confused:

olivia: thanks. do we have a request id or example response body? any logs from the api-proxy?

tara: pasted a trimmed sample from their error: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z
Request-Id: req_0a1b2c3d
Body: {"error":"quota_exhausted","detail":"monthly token bucket empty"}
```

kai: quick check — can you curl our credits endpoint for that org and share headers? `curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/orgs/acme-inc/credits"`

tara: ran from support vm, result: 
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Quota-Window: 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z/2026-04-01T00:00:00Z
X-Remaining-Tokens: 0
X-Cache-Source: shared-cache
Body: {"available":0}
```

edmond: hmmm X-Cache-Source is interesting. Our quota service publishes the refreshed monthly balance at 00:00 UTC, but streaming/proxy keeps a per-connection cached snapshot for efficiency. If a long-lived websocket connection had an expired local snapshot it might still route using the pre-refresh cached balance until reconnection — could explain why ongoing streams hit 429 while a fresh credits call shows the new window.

olivia: customer said the app had several long-running chat streams opened from yesterday that they never reconnected. they saw the 429s on those streams while new requests from the web UI succeeded after refresh.

tara: repro steps I used locally to mimic: 
1) open websocket to /v1/stream with token that returns cached credits=0 (simulate cache TTL >1h)
2) call `POST /v1/admin/force-window-refresh org=acme-inc` (internal debug) to trigger new monthly window
3) send message on websocket -> 429 from proxy
4) close+reopen websocket -> allowed (new credits visible)

kai: that matches. root cause likely: cache snapshot TTL + our streaming proxy consults cached balance and doesn't revalidate on window boundary. Edge-case: when the server-side refresh moves to a new window, the proxy should invalidate in-flight snapshots immediately. I can sketch a patch to have the refresh broadcast include a per-tenant revision that forces proxy invalidation.

edmond: short term mitigation: ask affected customers to reconnect streams. longer-term: change cache behavior so monthly-window flip sends invalidation event to connection layer. Also add an alert if X-Quota-Window header changes while a connection is open.

olivia: will reply to ACME with repro + suggested workaround (reconnect streams, or schedule a short rolling restart of workers if many persistent connections). Also asked for the list of request ids from their 00:00 timeframe — tara pasted them to the ticket. :white_check_mark:

tara: assigning to kai for the patch + edmond for alerting runbook updates. i'll mark the support ticket as "engineering escalation" and link here. thanks all. :thumbsup:
